title: Giuseppe Torri
text:
I’m an atmospheric scientist at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. My research group works on cumulus convection, severe weather, and the dynamics that link small-scale cloud processes to high-impact events — flash floods, lightning, wildfires.
This site is the informal companion to my lab page — CV, publications, and group info live there. Here you’ll find notes on models and methods, code, talks, and whatever I’m currently chasing.
Ciao, vecchio pirata. 🏴‍☠️

title: Welcome to the notebook
text:
This is where I’ll post short, informal notes — a neat result from a simulation, a debugging story, a paper I liked and why, conference takeaways. Nothing here is peer-reviewed; treat it as a lab notebook, not a publication.
For the group’s actual publications, CV, and research overview, see the main lab site.
A quick example of embedding code and a figure directly in a post:

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

x = np.linspace(0, 4 * np.pi, 200)
plt.plot(x, np.sin(x))
plt.xlabel("x")
plt.ylabel("sin(x)")
plt.show()
